children: Foreign investors heavily sold Japanese stocks in the week through September 12, as surging oil prices and rate-hike expectations in the United States and Japan prompted caution.
Foreign outflows stood at a net 1.52 trillion yen ($9.74 billion) last week, their largest weekly net sales since June 27, Ministry of Finance data showed.
fell 1.55% last week as oil prices surged about 8.65%, fueling inflation concerns. Benchmark Brent crude futures
touched a four-month high of $109.97 a barrel during the week.
On Wednesday, the U.S. Federal Reserve unanimously raised interest rates by 25 basis points to the 3.75% to 4.00% range, and the Bank of Japan is all but certain to lift interest rates on Friday.
Foreign investors, meanwhile, made net purchases of 2.24 trillion yen in Japanese long-term bonds—the largest weekly amount since April 4—while selling a net 1.21 trillion yen in short-term bills.

Japanese investors recorded a second straight week of net buying in foreign long-term bonds, purchasing a net 1.08 trillion yen, and also bought a net 150.8 billion yen in short-term debt instruments.
They also bought about 169.2 billion yen in foreign stocks, following net sales of roughly 481.6 billion yen the previous week.
